critical_steps: The original identical coordinate families are \(K\)-woven with exact \(K\)-relative lower bound \(C=16\) and Bessel bound \(D_\Gamma=1\).
The printed smallness quantity equals \(8\), below the printed threshold \(16\).
A mixed partition of the transformed families duplicates the first coordinate and annihilates \(e_2\), so no positive lower \(K\)-\(g\)-frame bound exists.
Taking square roots at the coefficient-norm step produces \(\sqrt C\) and \(\sqrt{D_\Gamma}\), yielding the repaired threshold and lower bound.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact two-dimensional coordinate \(g\)-frames, a scalar \(K\), and a unitary coordinate swap.
integrity.unproved_limits: No optimal perturbation threshold beyond the repaired sufficient condition is asserted.

scientific_limitations: The finding corrects Theorem 2.6 and does not reassess unrelated results in the article.
The square-root threshold is a sufficient repair obtained from the intended norm argument; it is not claimed to be globally optimal.
The counterexample uses the permitted scale freedom \(K=\frac14 I_H\); additional external normalizations on \(K\) could change how the printed and repaired thresholds compare.
A nonindexed erratum, thesis remark, or informal correction may contain the same observation.
title: A square-root scaling defect breaks a two-operator \(K\)-\(g\)-weaving theorem
